memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now the famine was still severe in the land. So when they had eaten all the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, 'Go back and buy us a little more food.'" - Gen 43:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The grain from Egypt has run out, and the famine grinds on. Jacob, who had stubbornly refused to send Benjamin back to Egypt (Gen 42:38), now finds his hand forced by simple need: "Go back and buy us a little more food." Hunger has a way of overruling our reluctance. What Jacob would not do out of trust, he must now do out of necessity.

There is a familiar pattern here. Sometimes we resist a step God is clearly leading us toward — out of fear, pride, or comfort — and we dig in our heels. Then life presses in, and the very circumstances we dreaded push us to do what we should have done all along. Need can be a stern but effective teacher.

We should not miss the mercy in this. Even our hardships can be used by God to move us where He wants us. The famine that emptied Jacob's barns was also the pressure that would ultimately reunite him with the son he thought was dead. God can use our times of need to nudge us onto the very path of blessing we were resisting.

Is there a step you have been avoiding, only to find that circumstances are now pressing you toward it? Rather than resenting the pressure, consider that God may be using it to lead you. Sometimes the empty barn is God's gentle push toward the provision we could not see.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a step I've resisted that circumstances are now forcing?
2. Can I see God's hand even in the pressures pushing me forward?
3. What might God be leading me toward through my present need?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I resist the path You are leading me down, use even my times of need to move me forward. Help me to see Your hand in the pressures of life, and to trust where You are leading. Amen.
